articles.author: Joey
articles.description:
AI video prompts can look completely reasonable and still produce a result that is not what you expected.
I ran into this while testing a skiing video.
The skier moved downhill correctly, the snow reacted to the skis, and the overall scene looked good. The problem was the camera. I wanted it to move in behind the skier, come closer, pass near the subject, and then pull away.
Instead, it barely moved.
My prompt included the phrase "dynamic tracking shot," so at first I thought the model had simply ignored the camera instruction. But when I looked at the prompt again, I realized that I had not actually described the camera movement in much detail.
That test changed the way I write AI video prompts.
I now spend less time adding descriptive words and more time separating the different kinds of…

articles.author: Henry Godnick
articles.description:
Most launch posts ask people to read a paragraph, click a landing page, and maybe remember the product later.
That is fine, but it is also a little passive.
For BuilderBench, I wanted the discovery loop to feel more like a founder side quest:
Play eight quick events.
Get one all-round score.
If you land in the top five, your SaaS link shows on the leaderboard.
The events are simple skill tests: Reaction Time, Sequence Memory, Aim Trainer, Number Memory, Verbal Memory, Chimp Test, Visual Memory, and Typing.
No pitch deck. No paid placement. No promise that a leaderboard spot magically turns into customers. Just a free game where builders can compete for a visible SaaS link instead of submitting another static launch blurb.
I like this format because it gives non-users a reason to interact before they care about the product. The product is not just being announced. It is giving people a tiny challenge they can try in under a few minutes.
That feels more fun than "please check out my SaaS."
If you are building something, try it here: https://www.buildersbenchmark.com/
Curious if other founders here have tried making their launch page interactive instead of purely informational.
articles.title: Your SaaS launch should have a high-score table
